messages:
alex: Heads-up — we need a concise playbook for the model introspection/discovery endpoint and capability flags. Goal: make launch gating & prioritization explicit for product + eng.

maria: +1. Are we focusing on runtime flags (streaming, kv-cache, token limits) or the whole surface (function-calling, structured output, embeddings)?

alex: Both, but split into two tiers: 1) runtime capabilities that affect routing & fallbacks (streaming, max_tokens, streaming formats), 2) API features (functions, JSON schema output, rerank/embeddings).

sam: I can draft a recommended response shape for discovery. Quick sketch:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-3b",
  "capabilities": ["chat","completions","embeddings","rerank","function-calling"],
  "features": {
    "streaming": {"supported": true, "format": "chunked-ndjson", "max_concurrent_streams": 8},
    "structured_output": {"supported": true, "schema": "json-schema/v1"},
    "max_input_tokens": 32768,
    "max_output_tokens": 8192
  },
  "tools": ["http_call","file_read","search"],
  "compatibility": ["kv-cache","quantized-weights"]
}
```

jordyn: Love the sketch. A few asks from sales: need explicit per-feature stability score and known regressions, and a customer-visible fallback mapping (e.g., if streaming false -> fallback to chunked-polling endpoint).

kevin: For launch gates we should require:
- discovery endpoint returns canonical schema with versioning
- streaming contract doc + error codes
- fallback behavior documented and tested
- token limits surfaced and tested end-to-end
- telemetry hooks for feature usage

alex: Agree. Also require canary tests for feature flags (rollout paths when a flag flips).

maria: Prioritization thoughts:
- P0: streaming + max_token guarantees + fallback mapping (affects most customers)
- P1: function-calling discovery + structured-output schema declaration
- P2: detailed tool manifest (per-model tool support) + stability scores

sam: Implementation note: discovery endpoint should be cheap and cacheable. Response should include "cache_ttl_secs" so client SDKs can avoid frequent probes.

introspect-bot: automated-check: discovery-schema-v1 validated for redwood-3b, redwood-13b. All checks passing.

jordyn: We need a simple migration story for customers when we change a capability flag. Proposal: add "deprecated_in" and "removed_in" fields and a recommended migration snippet.

maria: Example migration snippet for streaming -> polling fallback:
```js
if (!capabilities.streaming.supported) {
  // use pollChunksUntilComplete(model, input)
}
```

kevin: Also track metrics we care about for gating: percent of requests hitting fallback, average additional latency when fallback occurs, regression rate on structured-output validations.

alex: Action items:
- sam: produce final discovery JSON schema + examples for chat/completions/embeddings by EOD Fri (2005008000).
- maria: write launch gates checklist and minimal docs for fallbacks by Mon.
- jordyn: coordinate with sales for stability score rubric and migration messaging.
- kevin: propose telemetry events & canary test plan.

sam: noted. will include cache_ttl and versioning fields.

alex: Thanks. We'll use this thread as the short-form playbook draft. If anyone has a hot objection to the P0/P1/P2 breakdown, shout now. :thumbsup:

maria: :thumbsup:

kevin: no objections

jordyn: one small ask — include explicit example for rerank discovery (format + cost estimate).

alex: good call. add it to sam's scope.

introspect-bot: reminder: run schema-lint after updates.
